source_user: Advanced cluster case GDS-125: Evaluate GPUDirect Storage for checkpoint and dataset I/O in distributed training. Variant 125 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate storage throughput from GPU DMA, validate filesystem and kernel support, measure queue depth and tail latency, compare CPU-staged I/O, and test restart consistency after interruption. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Design a staged architecture rather than assuming disaggregation is beneficial. Define prefill workers as the owners of prompt computation and decode workers as the owners of token generation; specify where KV blocks live, how ownership and versioning are represented, and when blocks are evicted. Assume a long-context workload and multi-node RDMA fabric, but treat GPU, NIC, PCIe/NUMA topology, software versions, memory capacity, and Mooncake implementation details as unknown until inventoried. Record prefill/decode ownership, request and prompt-length distributions, KV block size and precision, replication, placement policy, eviction/TTL policy, batching, concurrency, and admission limits.

The falsifiable hypothesis is that remote KV placement improves the selected service objective (for example, decode inter-token latency or throughput at a stated load) versus the colocated/local baseline by a predeclared margin, without violating p99 latency, error, freshness, or recovery SLOs. Measure TTFT, inter-token latency, end-to-end latency, tokens/s, request throughput, queueing time, KV hit/miss and eviction rates, bytes and time per RDMA transfer, PCIe/NIC utilization, GPU utilization/memory, CPU use, queue depth, retries, and p50/p95/p99 distributions. Use synchronized timestamps and explicit ms, GiB/s, tokens/s, and percentage units; report per-node/rank skew and uncertainty, not only averages.

Validate RDMA reachability, registration and protection settings, topology/NUMA affinity, congestion and MTU/QoS configuration, and actual transfer traces. Separate network transfer time from compute and queueing time. Test cache consistency with request cancellation, duplicate/retried fetches, model/version changes, partial writes, and eviction races; a stale or wrong KV must never silently affect output. Admission control should bound remote-cache occupancy, outstanding RDMA work, and tail amplification, with backpressure and a bounded fallback to local recomputation or conventional serving.

For resilience, use leases or ownership epochs, checksums/version metadata where appropriate, idempotent fetches, bounded timeouts, and health-aware placement. During an authorized isolated drill, kill a cache node and interrupt an RDMA transfer; verify in-flight requests either retry from a valid version or recompute locally, no corrupted KV is reused, capacity is reclaimed, and service recovers within the stated SLO. Roll back to the local/conventional path if support or direct-transfer evidence is absent, p99 or error budgets regress beyond the predeclared gate, stale-KV correctness checks fail, or recovery exceeds the SLO. Do not claim a Mooncake benefit from architecture diagrams or aggregate throughput alone; require repeated matched runs, traces, logs, and recovery results.
risks: Actual Mooncake semantics, RDMA support, topology, and cache consistency guarantees are deployment-specific and unverified.
Remote KV can trade memory savings for RDMA latency, congestion, tail amplification, or stale/corrupt state.
Fault injection and production changes require authorization and isolated test data.

Matched local/conventional versus disaggregated repeated measurements with units, distributions, and uncertainty
